sessions.topic: Reporting Manager feature + Maternity leave + Admin request notifications

messages.content: Feature request (Telugu): Add Reporting Manager dropdown when admin adds employee; employee profile should show reporting manager name + ID; when an employee raises a leave/WFH/query request it should go to their reporting manager (not admin) by default; add Maternity Leave with 0 days; admin sidebar should show a notification when an employee raises a request.

Analyzed the codebase: employees table (server/schema.sql) had no reporting_manager_id column; roles include manager; leave_types already had Maternity Leave (180 days, female only); manager role existed but no manager approval UI; /api/notifications/counts bell already counted pending leaves/tickets for admin.

Asked clarifying questions. User chose: (1) New dedicated 'My Team' page for managers to approve leave/WFH and respond to queries; (2) Manager decision is final (admin/hr can still view/cancel/override); (3) Employees/managers without a reporting manager cannot apply for leave/WFH (error); (4) Maternity Leave = 0 days balance, shown as 0, no deduction, still approvable, never negative.

steps: DB (server/schema.sql): added reporting_manager_id to employees, leave_applications, wfh_requests, support_tickets (CREATE + idempotent ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + indexes); Maternity Leave days_per_year -> 0; leave balance clamps remaining with Math.max(0, days_per_year - used).

Server employees.js: LEFT JOIN self for reporting_manager_name/reporting_manager_employee_id on list/get; POST/PUT accept reporting_manager_id; PUT uses CASE to allow clearing RM without breaking other callers; self-RM blocked.
Server auth.js /me: returns reporting_manager_name + reporting_manager_employee_id.
Server leave.js + wfh.js POST /apply: employee/manager must have reporting_manager_id else 400 'No reporting manager assigned'; snapshots RM id into the request. Admin/hr exempt.
Server tickets.js POST /: snapshots reporting_manager_id (no block).

New server/routes/manager.js (mounted /api/manager, isManager): GET /team, GET /leaves, GET /wfh, GET /tickets (only direct reports, pending/open); PUT /leaves/:id and /wfh/:id approve/reject (final, marks attendance on leave approval); PUT /tickets/:id respond/resolve.
Server notifications.js: new GET /api/notifications/requests (admin) returning latest pending leave/WFH/ticket feed with employee name, type, dates, and links.

Frontend admin/employees.html: 'Reporting Manager' select in Add + Edit modals (populated from /api/employees?limit=1000&status=active, excludes admins), RM column in table, RM row in detail modal Employment section.
Frontend employee/profile.html: Reporting Manager shown in profile header and Job Details.

Frontend employee/leave.html + wfh.html: RM-not-assigned warning banner hides Apply button; approver name shown in apply modal; 0-day leave types shown as 'Special leave / no deduction'; apply blocked client-side without RM.
Frontend employee/dashboard.html: 0-day leave balance shown in neutral color.

New public/pages/manager/my-team.html: manager portal with team member chips, stat cards, tabs (Leave / WFH / Queries), approve/reject with remarks modal, ticket respond modal. Sidebar 'My Team' link injected for role=manager via dashboard.js loadManagerNav().

Frontend admin bell: dashboard.js initAdminNotificationPanel() turns the admin bell into a dropdown showing the pending-requests feed (leave/WFH/queries) linking to admin pages; badge count now includes pendingTickets.
verification: Ran idempotent DB migration directly against production Supabase (full schema re-run failed on pre-existing seed FK conflict). Columns added on all 4 tables; Maternity Leave days_per_year = 0 confirmed.
Production roster: only 3 employees (Admin id=1, terminated employee id=7, manager G0003 id=8). No RMs assigned - left to admin via new UI.

Smoke test (node + signed JWT): /api/auth/me 200, /api/notifications/requests 200 (empty feed), /api/employees 200 with RM join, /api/leave/types 200, /api/manager/team 200, /api/manager/leaves 200, /api/leave/balance 200 (clamp ok), POST /api/leave/apply without RM -> 400 'No reporting manager assigned. Contact your administrator.'

sessions.topic: Multi-level approval hierarchy with per-designation Team Leads (Employee -> Team Lead -> Manager -> HR -> Admin)

messages.content: Wants the approval chain to match a real office: employee requests go to their Team Lead (okko designation ki okkokaru - one TL per designation), TL leaves go to Manager, Manager leaves go to HR, HR to Admin, Admin is top. Confirm/refine the plan and implement 1 by 1.

Locked the chain as Employee -> Team Lead -> Manager -> HR -> Admin. Routing stays on the single reporting_manager_id (immediate supervisor) introduced in the prior session, so requests already flow one level up. New team_lead role added; team leads become approvers via isManager; Designation -> TL auto-assign; chain-aware 'Reporting To' dropdown; approver names shown in history. User approved, then said 'do it 1 by 1'.
steps: DB (server/schema.sql): role CHECK now includes 'team_lead'; idempotent migration block adds designations.team_lead_id FK (ON DELETE SET NULL) + index and drops/recreates employees_role_check. Applied directly to production Supabase (schema re-run still fails on legacy seed FKs).
Server middleware/auth.js: isManager allowedRoles -> ['admin','hr','manager','team_lead'].
Server leave.js + wfh.js: needsManager now includes 'team_lead' (TL's own leave/WFH routes to their manager).
Server routes/designations.js: GET joins employees tl for team_lead_id / team_lead_name / team_lead_employee_id; POST and PUT accept team_lead_id (PUT uses CASE $4::text to allow clearing).

Server routes/employees.js: PUT now walks the reporting chain from the candidate RM and rejects any assignment that would create a cycle (400 'reporting cycle'); self-RM already blocked. Also fixed a latent bug where the pagination COUNT query used a fragile .replace() that never matched (newline in the SELECT) -> 500 when 0 non-admin employees exist; replaced with /SELECT[\s\S]*?FROM employees/.

Frontend admin/designations.html: Team Lead column + 'Team Lead' select in add/edit modal (populated with active team_lead-role employees); hint that new employees in the designation auto-assign to this TL.

Frontend admin/employees.html: 'Team Lead' role option in Add + Edit modals; team_lead badge color; chain-aware Reporting Manager dropdown (Employee->team_lead, Team Lead->manager, Manager->hr, HR->admin, Admin->top/none, current admin self-injected as HR candidate); designation select auto-fills Reporting Manager with that designation's TL for employee role; existing RM preserved on edit ('- current' option); hint text under the RM field.
Frontend js/dashboard.js: loadManagerNav() injects 'My Team' for manager/team_lead/hr; role label map shows 'Team Lead' instead of 'Team_lead'.
Frontend pages/manager/my-team.html: auth guard allows manager/team_lead/hr (API already filters by reporting_manager_id = me).
Frontend employee/profile.html: role display maps team_lead -> 'Team Lead'.
Frontend employee/leave.html + wfh.html: needsRM includes team_lead; history tables add 'Approved By' column (approved_by_name). tickets.html already showed responded_by_name (no change needed).
verification: Targeted migration ran against production Supabase: designations.team_lead_id present, role CHECK includes team_lead.

End-to-end smoke test with temp users (manager -> team_lead -> employee chain), all 13 passed: GET /designations exposes team_lead fields; GET /employees?limit=1000 (count-query fix verified with 0 non-admin users); designation PUT team_lead_id reflected in GET; team_lead token passes /api/manager/team + /leaves and sees direct reports; /auth/me shows the TL as reporting_manager_name; cycle prevention + self-RM both reject 400; leave/apply with RM assigned proceeds (201). Temp users + designation permanently deleted afterwards (0 leftover confirmed).
Note: production roster is now down to a single Admin (id=1 EMP001) - the earlier id=7/id=8 employees were removed between sessions, so the smoke test could not rely on them.
